lesson.text: Quick memory: last unit, proportional relationships. If 3 pens cost 6 gold, what do 5 pens cost? 2 gold each, so 10 gold.
Percent increase or decrease = the change ÷ the original × 100. From 40 to 50 is a change of 10, and 10 ÷ 40 is 0.25: a 25% increase.
A discount takes a percent off; tax or a tip adds a percent on. 20% off 60 coins: 60 − 12 = 48 coins.
Simple interest: principal × rate × years. 200 gold at 5% for 3 years earns 200 × 0.05 × 3 = 30 gold.
Always compare with the original amount, not the new one.
Try it in the world: pick an item in the Gold Shop and work out 20% off its price, then a 10% rise. Always work from the original price. Next: expressions.

exercises.prompt: A price rises from 50 to 60 coins. What is the percent increase?
An 80-coin coat is 25% off. What is the sale price?
Simple interest is principal × rate × years.
exercises.hint: Look at the lesson's third card: which three things are multiplied?
exercises.explain: Yes: principal × rate × years, like 200 × 0.05 × 3 = 30 gold.

exercises.prompt: A town's buddies fall from 200 to 150. What is the percent decrease?
A 40-coin meal has a 15% tip added. What is the total?
A price goes up 10%, then down 10%. Compared with the start it is…
500 gold is saved at 4% simple interest a year. How much interest after 5 years?
exercises.explain: 4% of 500 is 500 × 0.04 = 20 gold a year. Simple interest is the same each year, so over 5 years: 20 × 5 = 100 gold.

exercises.prompt: After a 20% discount a game costs 32 coins. What was the original price?
exercises.explain: 20% off leaves 80% of the price, so 32 coins is 0.8 of it. 32 ÷ 0.8 = 40 coins. Check: 20% of 40 is 8, and 40 − 8 = 32.

exercises.prompt: Match each change to its percent.
exercises.hint: Find the change, then divide by the original.
exercises.explain: 50 to 60: 10 ÷ 50 is a 20% increase. 200 to 150: 50 ÷ 200 is a 25% decrease. 40 to 50: 10 ÷ 40 is a 25% increase. 80 to 40: 40 ÷ 80 is a 50% decrease.

exercises.prompt: Sort the changes: does the price go up or down?
exercises.hint: Discounts and sales take off; tax and tips add on.
exercises.explain: A tip and tax add on, so the price goes up. A discount, 20% off and a sale price take off.

exercises.prompt: A 60-coin jacket is 20% off. Then 10% tax is added to the sale price. How many coins do you pay?
exercises.hint: Take the discount off first, then add the tax to the new price.
exercises.explain: 20% of 60 is 12, so the sale price is 60 − 12 = 48 coins. 10% of 48 is 4.8, so you pay 48 + 4.8 = 52.8 coins: less than 60, but not 70% of it.
